newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney faces rising Olympic construction bill. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sydney faces rising Olympic construction bill. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]

text.p: The cost of constructing facilities for the Sydney 2000 Olympics has ballooned to A$3.2 billion (US$2.5 billion) since the city first bid for the Games in 1992, according to official figures released on Tuesday.
In its annual budget, the New South Wales state government said the public cost of building facilities has risen A$124 million in the past 12 months to A$2.1 billion.
On top of that, the private sector was to spend A$1.1 billion on the main Olympic stadium and village.

After adjusting for inflation, the original construction budget in Sydney's Olympic bid document in 1992 was A$2.55 billion, comprising A$1.59 billion state government expenditure and A$963 million private spending in 1997/98 dollar terms, the state government said in a statement.
(Correcting total for the original budget and making clear it has been expressed in 1997/98 dollar terms)
Unlike last year's Atlanta Games, entirely funded from commercial sources, the Sydney Olympics will be both underwritten by and effectively run by the state government.
Delivering the 1997-98 budget, NSW state treasurer Michael Egan said: "This is the budget that will break the back of Olympic construction expenditure.
"All of the Olympic construction costs are being paid for now, upfront. Not a cent will be left owing by September 2000."
The budget for the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) has also risen substantially.

New SOCOG budget figures will be released on Wednesday but SOCOG president and Olympics minister Michael Knight said last month its budget had grown to A$2.4 billion from an original estimate of A$1.7 billion.
Egan said the Olympic Coordination Authority (OCA), the state government authority charged with building Olympic infrastructure, will spend A$628.1 million in the year to June 30, 1998.
This will represent the biggest single slice spent in one year since Sydney won the right to host the Games in 1993.
Over three-quarters of the OCA's A$2.1 billion budget will be paid by state taxpayers. SOCOG, the federal government and other minor sources will provide A$513 million.

Opposition politicians, fearing a budget blowout, last month called for more regular and detailed reports of Olympics costs. A major factor in Sydney winning the Olympic bid was that the state government would underwrite the cost of the Games.

The organisers of the Atlanta Olympics struggled until the end of the Games to cover a US$1.7 billion budget, leading to accusations from within the Olympic movement that they had relied on tacky commercialism.
